subdomain: 1.4 Design multi-agent systems and orchestration strategies

en.question: A daily briefing has a fixed release deadline. Its mandatory core evidence is already verified; regional worker reports are optional supplements. Some regional searches stall. The business accepts missing supplements if omissions are disclosed, but it does not accept treating missing evidence as a negative finding. Which orchestration choices satisfy this contract? Select 3 answers.

options.text: Release the verified core by the deadline and disclose which optional supplements were unavailable.
options.note: The contract permits an explicitly incomplete supplement set. Publishing the valid core with disclosed omissions preserves both the deadline and the evidence boundary.

options.text: Collect optional worker results without requiring an all-worker completion barrier before publication.
options.note: An unconditional synchronous barrier makes release depend on the slowest optional worker. Removing that dependency allows useful parallel work without violating the core release requirement.

options.text: Wait for every regional search and retry stalled workers until each produces a complete report.
options.note: Unbounded waiting gives optional work control over the release deadline. The business explicitly permits omissions instead of requiring full regional completion.

options.text: Represent pending and failed supplements explicitly so synthesis cannot interpret silence as evidence of absence.
options.note: Typed task outcomes distinguish a failed search from a completed search with no finding. This prevents orchestration failures from becoming unsupported business conclusions.

references.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
